name: Monarch MK-V
def: Battery electric compact utility tractor with driver optional autonomy, sold for vineyards, orchards and dairies, with cameras for row following and safety.
body: The MK-V is a battery electric utility tractor sized for vineyard and orchard rows, rated at about 40 horsepower continuous with a 70 horsepower peak. It can be driven conventionally, driven by gesture and remote control, or left to run recorded rows on its own, with a camera ring watching for people and obstacles. Exportable electrical power lets it run electric implements. Farms use it for mowing, spraying, towing and hauling in California and elsewhere.
facts: Rated 40 horsepower continuous and 70 horsepower peak, with a 14 hour working day on a charge
Assembled in Livermore, California, with a manufacturing partnership with Foxconn in Ohio
Widely used in California wine grape vineyards and on dairies
specs: Four wheel drive battery electric tractor with a category one and two three point hitch
Battery electric with 5.6 kilowatts of exportable power
360 degree camera coverage with collision prevention and power take off protection
Driver optional operation with row following and gesture control; one operator can supervise up to eight tractors
